turns.t: Hi, doctor. I'm really sorry, I know it's probably just a cold, but I've been feeling awful for about ten days, and my sore throat's not going.
Let's have a look at the whole picture. Tell me what's been happening.
Sore throat, severe. I can barely swallow. And I'm exhausted, I sleep twelve hours and still wake up flattened.
When did it all start, as best you can say?
Um, a week and a half ago? Or maybe two weeks, I'm not sure. I think it was just after my flatmate's birthday.
That's fine. Any fever or sweats?
Fever, yes, on and off. But I haven't measured it.
Any rash?
No rash.
Any pain in your tummy, especially on the left side?
No. None.
Have you had any allergies to medicines?
Penicillin, I came out in a rash once, years ago, so I avoid it.
That's important. Do you know if anyone's had glandular fever in your house? ~
My flatmate had it last month. I'm a bit worried. ~
That's useful to know. Do you smoke or drink?
I vape sometimes, and drink at the weekend.
Any other conditions?
Asthma, mild.
Let me look at your throat. Open wide. ~
Ahh.
Your tonsils are swollen with a white coating on both, and the glands at the back of your neck are enlarged and tender.
Is it tonsillitis? ~
It could be, but with the exhaustion, swollen neck glands, and your flatmate's illness, I'd say glandular fever is more likely than ordinary tonsillitis.
Oh no. How long does that last? ~
Often a few weeks, sometimes longer. I can't rule out a bacterial throat infection on top, so I'd like to take a throat swab.
Right. ~
And I'd like to arrange blood tests, to check for the virus and your blood count.
Okay. And will I get antibiotics? ~
Not unless the swab shows bacteria, and with your history, I'd choose carefully. ~
Fair enough. ~
Rest, drink plenty, take paracetamol for the pain, and don't play contact sports, because your spleen may be enlarged.
I'll stay home. ~
If you can't swallow your saliva, have severe tummy pain on the left, or get a high fever, come in right away.
I will. Thank you. ~
